title.en: Ramayana — Uttara Kanda (The Story of the Later Ramayana — English, Full Text)

lessons.title: Lesson 01 — Rama's Reign (Ram Rajya)
lessons.content: After the coronation of Sri Rama, happiness and prosperity spread throughout Ayodhya. Under the rule of Sri Rama, the people lived without any hardship. That is why **Ram Rajya** is still cited as an example of an ideal state. One day, during a private moment, Rama approached Sita and asked, “Devi! You are going to be a mother. If you have any wish in your heart, tell me.” Sita replied, “My Lord, I wish to spend one day in the hermitages of the sages on the banks of the Ganga, subsisting on fruits and roots.” Rama agreed but became troubled upon hearing Sita's wish.

lessons.title: Lesson 02 — Slander Against Sita
lessons.content: From there, Rama went to the assembly hall, where Vijaya, Madhumatta, Kashyapa, Pingala, Kuta, Suraja, and others entertained him with humorous stories. Pleased, Rama asked Bhadra, “Bhadra! How is my administration? Do the people have any problems? Tell me the truth.” Bhadra replied, “Maharaja! I will tell you the truth, as you are a truth-speaker. The people praise your valor and the slaying of Ravana highly. However, they are discussing and saying various things about you accepting Sita back as your wife after she spent some time in Ravana's captivity. Please forgive me for saying this.” Rama accepted his words and dismissed everyone. Filled with sorrow, he called for his younger brothers. Seeing Rama's face, they were stunned. Rama asked them to sit down and explained everything that had happened. “Lakshmana! Even the Sun, Moon, Agni, and Indra praised her character. But the **slander against her** has not been cleared in Ayodhya. A rule that does not have the people's favor is like a day without the sun. Now, I see no other way but to abandon her. A little while ago, Sita requested to visit the hermitages of the sages, and I granted her permission. **Do not argue, take her to the hermitages on the banks of the Ganga river and leave her there. This is my command**,” he ordered.

lessons.title: Lesson 03 — Sita Banished to the Forest
lessons.content: Lakshmana, without a word, instructed the minister Sumantra to prepare the chariot early in the morning. He then went to Sita and said, “Mother. As per your wish to spend time in a hermitage, my brother has commanded me to take you to the hermitages on the banks of the Ganga river today.” Sita happily set out with him for the Ganga. After crossing the river, on the bank near the sage's hermitage, he revealed the truth, “Mother! Forgive my sin. I brought you here only to **abandon you on this bank**, not to take you back to Ayodhya.” Sita fainted, and upon recovering, she said, “O Soumitri! It seems I was born only to suffer hardships. The sin of a previous birth must indeed follow me. Earlier, I lived in the forests with my husband's support. Can I live alone now? What answer should I give to the sages' wives who ask why my husband abandoned me? Nevertheless, I must endure my fate. Tell him that I respect his command. Convey my salutations.” Lakshmana bowed to her feet, circled her, and, unable to leave, crossed the Ganga river and departed.

lessons.title: Lesson 04 — The Sage's Hermitage and Lava-Kusha
lessons.content: Sita remained there until he left, crying loudly and collapsing. Valmiki, the sage, learned of this through his young disciples, brought her to his hermitage, and consoled her: “My child! You are the **daughter of Janaka, the daughter-in-law of Dasaratha, and the wife of Rama**. You are supremely virtuous. I know everything through my ascetic power. You remain without worry. All the wives of the sages here will look after you as their own daughter.” He called everyone in his hermitage by name and entrusted them with the responsibility of ensuring Janaki Devi suffered no hardship. After some time there, Janaki Devi gave birth to **two boys**. Named **Lava and Kusha**, they grew day by day, excelling in both Vedic knowledge and martial arts.

lessons.title: Lesson 05 — The Ashwamedha Yaga (Sacrifice)
lessons.content:
Meanwhile, one day, Rama called his brothers and told them he wished to perform the **Rajasuya Yaga**, seeking their advice. Bharata paid his respects to his elder brother and said, “Lord! Under your rule, Dharma is perfectly upheld. Your fame is like the moonlight clinging to the moon. There are no sinful kings. Have you forgotten that you are the protector and refuge for all creatures on this earth? The Rajasuya Yaga causes the downfall of many royal lineages. Therefore, I believe the Rajasuya Yaga is unnecessary.” Lakshmana then interjected, “Brother! What Bharata said is one hundred percent true and righteous. Since you desire to perform a sacrifice, perform the **Ashwamedha Yaga**. Indra performed this in the past to absolve himself of the sin of Brahmahata (Brahmanicide) caused by slaying Vritrasura.” Sri Rama was pleased with their words. “Brothers, your words are agreeable to me. Make the necessary arrangements to conduct this sacrifice,” he permitted.

Kings like Sugriva and Vibhishana, sages, actors, singers, and scholars arrived. A magnificent sacrificial altar was built on the bank of the Gomati river in the **Naimisharanya** forest, with all facilities provided for the attendees. Rama worshipped a horse with good characteristics and set it free. **Lakshmana**, along with the ritual priests (Ritvijas), set out as its protector. Rama then entered the sacrificial enclosure. All the kings on earth congratulated Rama and offered gifts. Thus, the prestigious Ashwamedha Yaga continued for a year. Everyone praised it. At that time, **Sage Valmiki** arrived with his disciples. Bharata and Shatrughna specially constructed a comfortable hermitage for him and arranged his stay. After settling in, Valmiki seated Lava and Kusha and instructed them: “My long-lived ones! Sing the Ramayana I taught you melodiously, in tune, and sweetly on the royal roads, in the sages' dwellings, and near Rama's assembly at the Yajna site. Sing twenty cantos a day. Eat only fruits and roots. **Do not accept any wealth if offered**. If anyone asks who you are, say only that you are the **disciples of Valmiki**. And do not look down upon the Lord, Sri Rama,” he advised.

lessons.title: Lesson 06 — The Singing of the Ramayana
lessons.content: The next morning, Lava and Kusha paid their respects to Sage Valmiki, received his blessings, and began singing the Ramayana throughout Ayodhya. The people were enchanted by the sweetness of the song and followed them. The melody of Lava and Kusha's singing was the topic of discussion everywhere. Rama, too, was mesmerized upon hearing the song. As soon as the Yaga rituals were complete, Rama convened an assembly where sages, kings, scholars, musicians, linguists, Vedic experts, and all masters of knowledge were seated, and he requested Lava and Kusha to present their melodious song. They beautifully sang twenty cantos, from the first one. The assembly members clapped and cheered for the sweetness of their singing. Rama asked Bharata to present the boys with eighteen thousand gold coins, but **Lava and Kusha refused**, saying they did not need any wealth or gifts. Rama then asked, “What is the epic you sang?” Lava and Kusha replied, “Its author is **Sage Valmiki**. He is here now. He is our guru. He wrote your story in **twenty-four thousand verses**. It has 7 Kandas (books), five hundred Sargams (cantos), and one hundred stories. If you desire it, we will continue to sing and tell you.”

lessons.title: Lesson 07 — Janaki (Sita) is Stainless
lessons.content:
Rama agreed. As per his request, they continued to sing the Ramayana every day. Hearing it, Rama realized that they were indeed Sita's sons. He immediately summoned messengers and told them to go to Valmiki and convey his words: “O Great Sage! Rama respectfully submits this to you: I have heard your epic, and it is exceedingly beautiful. If you truly believe that **Janaki Devi is stainless**, you must bring her before the assembly so she can prove that fact.” They met Valmiki and returned, saying, “Sita will declare her innocence tomorrow. Valmiki has said that even those who cast aspersions on her can attend the assembly.” Rama addressed the assembly, “Tomorrow, Sita will proclaim her innocence. You must all attend.” Upon hearing his declaration, everyone praised him, saying, “Only you can uphold such righteous governance.” When Sita entered the assembly, all the attendees, including Sri Rama, respectfully stood up and then resumed their seats with the permission of the sage. The people wept upon seeing Janaki Devi, a personification of graceful beauty, after a long time. Then, breaking the profound silence, Valmiki spoke in a voice as deep as a cloud: “O Assembly members! This is **Janaki Devi**, the supremely virtuous wife of Sri Ramachandra, the daughter-in-law of Dasaratha. Sri Ramachandra abandoned her out of fear of public slander. What I say is the **truth**. If there is any falsehood in my words, the power of my penance, accumulated over thousands of years, will be nullified.”

The assembly members were stunned by the great sage's words. Sri Rama rose with a faint smile, calming the sage, and said, “O King of Sages! Your divinely-wise words are a truthful ornament. I have no doubt whatsoever about the chastity of my wife. I know she is a great virtuous woman. But it was necessary for the people to know this too, which is why I acted as I did. Furthermore, my inner self tells me that these boys are my own sons. **Sita must declare her virtue for the sake of the world**,” he stated. At those words, everyone looked towards Sita.

lessons.title: Lesson 08 — Sita Enters the Earth
lessons.content: Sita, dressed in ochre robes, looked once at the assembly. She joined her hands in prayer. A cool, sweet fragrance began to spread in the air of the assembly hall. Then Sita said, “If I have thought of none but **Rama**, may Mother Earth make a path for me to enter. If I have always worshipped Rama with purity in my thought, word, and deed (**Trikaraṇa Śuddhi**), may Mother Earth show me the way to enter.” As soon as Sita Devi finished her prayer, the earth split open. A divine throne, carried by the **Naga kings**, rose up. Mother Earth, seated on it, took Sita with both hands and lovingly held her beside her. As a rain of flowers fell from the sky, the throne descended into the netherworld, and the earth closed up as if nothing had happened. The assembly members looked at Rama, weeping in distress. Rama's grief was immeasurable. “My wife vanished right before my eyes. If I could bring her back from Lanka, can I not bring her back from the earth? O Mother Earth! I, your son-in-law, politely ask you. If you do not immediately bring Sita to me, **I will cause a cosmic deluge (Jagath Praḷaya)**,” he said. Brahma then intervened, saying, “Rama! This is not fitting for you. You will surely meet her in your heavenly abode. Your story will remain as an epic. You have heard what has transpired until now. The great sage has also written what is yet to come. Only you and the sages should hear it,” and he departed.

lessons.title: Lesson 09 — Lakshmana's Moral Dilemma
lessons.content: The next day, Rama listened to the remaining story. The Ashwamedha Yaga concluded. Rama returned to Ayodhya with Lava and Kusha. Time waits for no one. One day, a sage came and asked to see Rama, and Lakshmana, upon Rama's order, admitted the sage to Rama's private chamber. The sage said, “Rama! The matters we discuss must not be known to any outsider. If anyone enters or overhears, you must **punish them with death**, then only will I converse with you.” Rama agreed and asked Lakshmana to guard the door. The sage then said, “Ramachandra! I am not a sage. **I am Yama, the God of Death**. I am the dispenser of timely death to humans. The purpose for which you came to this world is fulfilled. Brahma has requested you to return and rule the higher worlds.” Rama smiled and replied, “O Yama! My duty is to protect the three worlds. I am preparing to return to my original abode.” While they were conversing, **Durvasa**, the short-tempered sage, came to see Rama. Lakshmana requested a delay for the audience. Durvasa, known for his anger, shouted, “Oh! Should I wait for Rama's audience? I must meet Rama immediately. Otherwise, I will curse your kingdom, your lineage, and your brothers to be destroyed!” Lakshmana, knowing Durvasa's wrath, considered that it would be better for **him to receive the death sentence** by defying Rama's command than for his lineage and kingdom to be destroyed. Thus, he interrupted the conversation between Yama and Rama, saying, “Brother! Sage Durvasa has arrived for you.”

lessons.title: Lesson 10 — Lakshmana's Yoga Samadhi
lessons.content:
Rama quickly sent Yama away and went out to welcome Durvasa. Durvasa requested a sumptuous meal, as he was hungry. After satisfying his request, Rama recalled the promise he had made to Yama and was overcome with sorrow. Lakshmana approached him and said, “Brother! You must not break your word. **Execute the punishment without hesitation** and uphold Dharma,” encouraging him. Rama was deeply distressed and summoned Vasishtha, Bharata, and Shatrughna to discuss the matter. Vasishtha advised, “O King! You must not break your word. **You should exile Lakshmana**.” Rama told Lakshmana, “Since abandoning a virtuous person is equivalent to death, I am exiling you.” Immediately, Soumitri, without even looking back at his home, went straight to the bank of the **Sarayu River** and entered a **Yoga Samadhi** (deep meditative state). Indra took him to Amaravati in his divine chariot. The Devas rejoiced that the fourth part of Vishnu's incarnation had returned to them.

After exiling Lakshmana, Sri Rama announced that he would crown Bharata as king and then leave. The entire kingdom grieved upon hearing this. Bharata fainted. Recovering after a while, Bharata said, “Brother! What is a kingdom to me without you? I cannot live without you. Let us divide the kingdom of Kosala into two parts and give the South to **Kusha** and the North to **Lava**. This is righteous. Let us immediately send word to Shatrughna.” The sequence of events stunned the people. Vasishtha advised, “Rama! You must also consider the **will of the people** before making a decision.” The King held an assembly with the people and asked, “My decision is to renounce the kingdom and leave. What is your decision?” They replied, “Lord! Your decision is our command. Many of us wish to follow you. Please permit us. That is our wish.” Rama agreed.

lessons.title: Lesson 11 — Rama's Decision
lessons.content: That very day, Rama coronated Lava and Kusha, seated them on his lap, smelled their heads affectionately, gave them good counsel, and sent them off with wealth, gold, and chariots: **Kusha** to **Kushavati** and **Lava** to **Sravasti**. He then sent messengers to inform Shatrughna of all that had happened. Shatrughna called his ministers and priests and declared that he too would follow his elder brother. He divided his kingdom into two, crowned his elder son **Subahu** in **Mathura** and his younger son **Shatrughati** in **Vidisha Nagara**. Learning that Rama was leaving, Vanaras, bears (Bhallukas), and Rakshasas gathered in great numbers at Ayodhya. Angada joined his hands and said, “Rama! I have entrusted my kingdom to my son Angada. Take me with you too.” Vibhishana came to Rama and was about to say something, but Rama stopped him and commanded, “Vibhishana, as long as the Sun and Moon exist, and as long as my story is told in this world, **you must rule righteously** so that your governance is also praised. This is my command as a friend. Moreover, never cease to worship the Lord of the Universe, the deity of our Ikshvaku lineage.” He then called Hanuman and blessed him: “My son! You, Mainda, and Dwivida, the three of you, shall be **immortal (Chirayu)** until the end of the Kali Yuga.” He then granted permission for the remaining Vanara and bear warriors to accompany him.

lessons.title: Lesson 12 — End of Rama's Earthly Reign
lessons.content:
The next morning dawned. With Brahmanas leading the way, carrying the sacred fires (Agnihotras) and the Vajapeya umbrella, Rama walked, wearing simple clothes, holding Darbha grass between his fingers, and chanting mantras. Sri Devi (Goddess of Wealth) and Hri Devi (Goddess of Modesty) walked on his two sides, and Bhudevi (Mother Earth) walked in front. His bow and arrows followed him in human form. The Vedas, Gayatri, Omkara, and Vashatkaras (sacred chants) followed the ancient Purusha. Brahma-Rishis, scholars, Bharata, Shatrughna, the palace people, Vanaras, common folk, and Rakshasas followed the righteous Purushottama. Even the animals and birds in Ayodhya followed Rama, leaving Ayodhya empty and desolate. Sri Rama walked half a Yojana (about 4 miles) and reached the Sarayu River, which flows westward. By then, **Lord Brahma** was waiting there, seated with groups of sages and Devas. The sky was filled with divine chariots. Priests chanted mantras. The Devas sounded their drums (Dundubhis). The air blew cool with perfumes. A shower of flowers began. Then, Rama placed his foot into the Sarayu River. Brahma then said to Rama, “**O Mahavishnu!** May all be well with you! Along with your brothers, abandon your gross physical bodies and assume your **divine form (Divya Sharira)**. Take the form you desire, my child! You are the support for all worlds.”

Hearing the words of the Grandsire (Pitamahudu), **Rama assumed his Vaishnava form**. His brothers did the same. Kinnaras, Kimpurushas, Yakshas, and Devas from all worlds cheered and bowed with devotion to Vishnu. Vishnu then commanded Brahma, “All those who followed me are my devotees. They renounced everything to follow me. **Grant them the higher worlds (Puṇya Lokas)**.” Brahma bowed to Vishnu with folded hands and said, “Deva! Those who have faith in you and seek refuge in you, even if they are animals or birds, will reach the divine world of **Santanaka**. I will now send all of them to that world. The Vanaras will attain the divine aspect from which they were born. **Sugriva** will merge into the **Sun**.” Those who followed Rama dipped themselves in the holy ford called **Go Pratāram**. They abandoned their former bodies and gained divine ones. They then departed to the higher worlds in the chariots allotted to them.
